Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0116", "row_sha256": "d3155955f82ec30daeeca40d4952da519b034be4ec31cc0d320fe28dd8d90b8c", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
we need a prompt for a screen reader audit of the cedar county library online renewal portal, not a general accessibility review of the whole library site. the audit is for the renewal flow on the public test site before the team decides what to fix, and it should focus on what a screen reader user can perceive and do. the test build is called Juniper 2.4 and was refreshed on april 14. the public test site is separate from the live service, so make that distinction clear and don't imply that the findings describe the live portal. the audience for the resulting report is the library's product and web teams, who know the portal but may not know the audit setup.

please ask the auditor to examine the route from the account sign-in page through the item renewal confirmation. patrons enter a library card number and a password, reach the account page, find a list of checked-out items, choose one or more eligible items, and activate Renew selected. the portal then shows a status message and an updated due date for successfully renewed items. there is also a link back to the account overview. include the path for a renewal that cannot be completed, where the item is blocked by a hold or another eligibility rule, but don't assume how often that happens or what the interface says until it is tested. a patron can renew more than one item in the same visit, so the prompt should make room for both single-item and multi-item behavior.

the session is planned for the afternoon of may 6 in the library's small training room. the tester, Mara Ellis, uses NVDA with Firefox on a Windows 11 laptop and a standard keyboard; she will not use a mouse during the task. her screen is set to 150 percent zoom, and the laptop is connected to the library's guest network. note those conditions because they help explain the scope of the observations, but do not treat them as proof that other browsers, screen readers, zoom levels, or devices work or fail. we have not arranged a second tester or a second session. don't present this as a broad user study or a complete conformance evaluation.

the materials for the session are in the shared audit folder: the test account details, the task card, the current renewal policy excerpt, a blank observation sheet, and a screen capture from the test site. do not rename files. the audit coordinator has said, “We need to know where a patron loses the thread, not just whether a control has a label.” keep that quote as ordinary context from the coordinator rather than treating it as a required verdict. the auditor may add notes to a separate working copy of the observation sheet, and can refer to the policy excerpt when describing an eligibility message. don't change the supplied test account, and don't include its password in the report.

please have the auditor move through the task at a normal pace, reading the interface with NVDA and using keyboard commands to reach and operate controls. ask for observations about the order and clarity of headings, the names and roles of controls, the relationship between each item and its due date or renewal status, and whether the current keyboard position is understandable after an action. include what happens when a status message appears, whether it is announced without extra navigation, and whether the changed due date can be found again. for a blocked item, ask the auditor to note the message and available next step if one is shown; do not assume there is a particular remedy. record when an observation is uncertain or when the test does not cover a behavior.

1. structure the eventual report so the product and web teams can scan it. start with a short description of the test conditions and the route covered, then group observations by stage of the renewal flow rather than by the order in which the auditor happened to write notes. for each issue that is actually observed, include the page or step, what the tester did, what NVDA or the keyboard exposed, and the practical effect on completing or understanding a renewal. distinguish a direct observation from an interpretation, and avoid claiming a defect solely because a particular control was unfamiliar to the tester. use concise headings and concrete wording. this should be a report of the session, not code or a redesign proposal.

there may be differences between the task card and the policy excerpt, or the test site may not offer a particular state during the session. ask the auditor to identify that kind of gap in the report, rather than silently reconciling it or filling it with a guess. if something works as expected, it can be noted briefly where useful, but do not require a positive finding for every step. do not turn absence of an observation into a claim that the interface works. the team wants findings they can trace to what happened in this one session, not a score or a claim about all patrons.

please keep the report useful for the next review meeting, which is on may 13. the meeting is for discussing which observations need follow-up, not for announcing that fixes have been approved. mention the test build name and date so readers can identify what was examined, and keep the account credentials out of the report. the team may compare the notes with a later build, but no later build or comparison results are available now. finish with the session limits and any specific untested path that matters, including if the blocked-renewal state could not be reached. the final paragraph should give the reader distinct information about what this session did not establish, rather than repeating the opening scope.", "output": "Create a screen-reader audit report for the Cedar County Library online renewal portal. Limit the audit to the renewal flow on the public test site; do not describe it as a general review of the library site or imply that observations from the test site apply to the live service. The test build is Juniper 2.4, refreshed on April 14. Write for the library’s product and web teams, who know the portal but may not know the audit setup.

**Test conditions and scope**

The session is planned for the afternoon of May 6 in the library’s small training room. The tester, Mara Ellis, uses NVDA with Firefox on a Windows 11 laptop and a standard keyboard, without a mouse. The screen is set to 150 percent zoom, and the laptop is connected to the library’s guest network. State these conditions as context for the observations. They do not establish whether other browsers, screen readers, zoom levels, or devices work or fail. There is no second tester or second session, so do not characterize the work as a broad user study or a complete conformance evaluation.

Examine the route from the account sign-in page through the item renewal confirmation. Patrons enter a library card number and password, reach the account page, find their checked-out items, select one or more eligible items, and activate **Renew selected**. The portal then displays a status message and an updated due date for successfully renewed items, with a link back to the account overview. Include both single-item and multi-item behavior. Also examine the path when a renewal cannot be completed because an item is blocked by a hold or another eligibility rule. Do not assume how often this occurs or what the interface says before testing it.

**Session materials and procedure**

The shared audit folder contains the test account details, task card, current renewal policy excerpt, blank observation sheet, and a screen capture from the test site. Do not rename files. The auditor may add notes to a separate working copy of the observation sheet and may refer to the policy excerpt when describing an eligibility message. Do not change the supplied test account or include its password in the report.

Have the auditor work through the task at a normal pace, reading with NVDA and using keyboard commands to reach and operate controls. Observe the order and clarity of headings; the names and roles of controls; the relationship between each item and its due date or renewal status; and whether the current keyboard position is understandable after an action. Record what happens when a status message appears, whether it is announced without extra navigation, and whether the changed due date can be found again. If an item is blocked, note the message and any next step shown without assuming a particular remedy. Mark observations as uncertain when appropriate, and identify behavior the session does not cover.

The audit coordinator said, “We need to know where a patron loses the thread, not just whether a control has a label.” Treat this as ordinary context, not as a required verdict.

**Report organization**

Begin with a short description of the test conditions and route covered. Group observations by stage of the renewal flow, rather than by the order in which notes were written. For each issue actually observed, give the page or step, what the tester did, what NVDA or the keyboard exposed, and the practical effect on completing or understanding a renewal. Distinguish direct observation from interpretation; do not call something a defect solely because a control was unfamiliar to the tester. Use concise headings and concrete wording. Report the session; do not provide code or a redesign proposal.

If the task card and policy excerpt differ, or the test site does not offer a particular state during the session, identify the gap rather than silently reconciling it or guessing. A useful observation that something worked as expected may be noted briefly, but a positive finding is not required for every step. Do not treat an absent observation as proof that the interface works. Tie findings to what happened in this one session, not to a score or a claim about all patrons.

The report is for the May 13 review meeting, where the team will discuss which observations need follow-up; do not announce that fixes have been approved. Include the build name and refresh date so readers can identify what was examined, and keep account credentials out of the report. The team may compare notes with a later build, but no later build or comparison results are available now. In the final paragraph, state what this session did not establish and identify any specific untested path that matters, including whether the blocked-renewal state could not be reached. Provide distinct information there rather than repeating the opening scope."}]
